docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: Essential mortgage infrastructure with an impaired common security
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/310522/000031052213000065/fanniemae201210k.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/310522/000031052213000138/a2013q2pressrelease.htm
Date: 2013-08-08

Fannie Mae purchases and guarantees residential mortgages, issuing mortgage-backed securities that investors can trade without individually underwriting every borrower. It supports purchase, refinance and rental housing finance. Freddie Mac performs a broadly comparable role under a separate charter and capital structure.

Scale, lender relationships, underwriting data, servicing infrastructure and a liquid securities market are difficult to replicate quickly. These enterprises are important to the availability of long-term fixed-rate mortgages. That does not establish that their present common shareholders own an unrestricted claim to the resulting profits.

Fannie has operated in FHFA conservatorship since September2008. Treasury provides a contractual funding backstop in exchange for senior preferred interests and warrants. Management describes the company as managed in taxpayers' overall interest, not as an ordinary shareholder-controlled corporation. The government can pursue policy goals that conflict with common investors' returns.

The business has single-family, multifamily and capital-markets activities. Guarantee economics depend on fees, credit losses, operating costs and required capital; retained mortgage investments also have interest-rate and funding risk. Retained portfolios are subject to mandated reduction, so historical investment earnings are not automatically a sustainable growth business.

Fannie's June2013 single-family book is approximately US$2.84 trillion. A very small change in credit losses on a book of this scale matters. Newer underwriting and recovering home prices have improved credit quality, but the old crisis-vintage book still contributes losses and reserve uncertainty.

The annual report identifies higher guaranty fees on new acquisitions as a contributor to future profitability. A scaled franchise with repriced new business could have substantial economic value if privately capitalized. The missing bridge is the allocation of that value among Treasury, junior preferreds, new capital and today's common shares.

A common investment therefore contains at least two separate judgments: the franchise can continue to produce attractive earnings, and legal/political decisions will eventually allow existing common equity to participate. Strong operating results are necessary evidence for the first proposition, not sufficient proof of the second.

An activist cannot simply replace the CEO, win a proxy contest and stop the Treasury dividend. Conservatorship, statutory powers and the purchase agreements dominate the normal corporate-governance toolkit.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: A genuine recovery amplified by accounting and credit normalization
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/310522/000031052213000065/fanniemae201210k.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/310522/000031052213000065/fanniemae201210kex121.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/310522/000031052213000138/a2013q2pressrelease.htm
Date: 2013-08-08

US$ billions unless stated. These are Fannie figures, not combined GSE results.

| Metric | 2010 | 2011 | 2012 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Net income/(loss) | −14.018 | −16.855 | 17.220 |
| Treasury draws | 15.0 | 25.9 | 0 |
| Treasury dividends | 7.7 | 9.6 | 11.6 |

The 2012 annual report was filed in April2013. Consolidation rules changed in2010 and brought a large volume of securitization trusts onto the balance sheet; gross interest revenue, debt and assets should not be compared mechanically with pre-2010 reports. Traditional industrial-company EV/revenue and net-debt/EBITDA are poor measures here.

The recovery reflects improving housing conditions, lower credit costs and stronger new mortgage acquisitions. It is not equivalent to all earnings being distributable to common shareholders. Treasury dividends and senior priority dominate the capital waterfall.

Q2 2013 net interest income was US$5.667 billion and net revenue US$6.152 billion. Net income was US$10.1 billion and comprehensive income US$10.3 billion. Higher home prices reduced estimated losses and required reserves; fair-value gains also helped. Annualizing the entire quarterly profit would assume these benefits recur.

Q1 included a US$50.571 billion income-tax benefit associated with release of the deferred-tax-asset valuation allowance. This is a large accounting recognition of expected future tax benefits, not recurring annual franchise earnings and not an equivalent fresh common distribution.

At June30, net worth was US$13.2 billion. The September Treasury dividend was US$10.2 billion, leaving the contractual US$3 billion capital reserve. Treasury's senior preferred remained US$117.1 billion. Dividends do not repay its liquidation preference or extinguish warrants.

Fannie reported a Q2 net loss attributable to common holders of approximately US$159 million, US$0.03 diluted loss per share, despite its large enterprise profit. This is the central accounting clue against applying a low headline P/E to common.

Single-family serious delinquency fell from 3.29% at December2012 to 2.77% at June2013. Industrial-style free cash flow and maintenance capex are not supplied as valuation substitutes. The appropriate analysis needs normalized credit losses, guaranty fees, regulatory capital, senior claims and common dilution.
docs.D03_latest_results_and_benchmark.md:
Title: Both enterprises are profitable; neither common stock has normal distributions
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/310522/000031052213000138/a2013q2pressrelease.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1026214/000119312513323022/d554149dex991.htm
Date: 2013-08-08

The August releases cover Q2, the latest published quarter at the October31 cutoff. No November Q3 earnings or deferred-tax event is included.

| Q2 2013 | Fannie Mae | Freddie Mac |
|---|---:|---:|
| Net income, US$bn | 10.1 | 5.0 |
| Comprehensive income, US$bn | 10.3 | 4.4 |
| June30 net worth, US$bn | 13.2 | 7.4 |
| September Treasury dividend, US$bn | 10.2 | 4.4 |
| Treasury senior preferred, US$bn | 117.1 | 72.3 |
| Single-family serious delinquency | 2.77% | 2.79% |

Fannie's six consecutive profitable quarters and Freddie's seven show that improved results are not an isolated one-quarter event. Both attribute material benefits to improving credit and housing conditions. They remain exposed to changes in interest rates, house prices, reserve estimates and legacy claims.

Fannie says it expects to remain profitable for the foreseeable future, with stable revenues and strong annual earnings over the next few years. It also warns that quarterly earnings may vary significantly. This is management's outlook, not a commitment to distribute profits to common.

Freddie's deferred-tax valuation allowance was still US$28.6 billion at June30. That balance is a disclosed accounting item, not a completed release or a forecast amount that can be booked into the next quarter.

Freddie reports post-2008 loans at 70% of its single-family credit-guarantee portfolio, including relief refinance loans. The newer book supports improved credit performance but does not remove all housing risk. Its July US$500 million STACR transaction transfers a portion of credit risk to private investors, illustrating a possible role for private capital under conservatorship.

The two companies are useful operating and policy benchmarks for each other, but each has separate shares, preferred claims, lawsuits and economics. Buying both does not diversify the shared Treasury/FHFA policy decision.

No truly matched listed private comparator combines their scale, charter, funding support, mortgage-guarantee role and conservatorship. Commercial-bank P/E and private mortgage-insurer margins may inform pieces of a model but cannot justify a mechanical comparable multiple. The pack does not invent an ordinary listed-peer valuation table.
docs.D04_price_and_capital_waterfall.md:
Title: Low price, extreme volatility and a nonstandard denominator
Source: compiled from: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/FNMA?period1=1351641600&period2=1383264000&interval=1d; https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/FMCC?period1=1351641600&period2=1383264000&interval=1d; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/310522/000031052213000137/fanniemaeq20630201310q.htm
Date: 2013-10-31

Historical unadjusted closes on October31 are approximately US$2.34 for FNMA and US$2.24 for FMCC. Session volumes were approximately 29.58 million and 12.76 million respectively. Twenty-session average volumes calculated from the historical series are approximately 30.69 million and 13.82 million.

The series records one-year intraday highs around US$5.44 and US$5.00 respectively. An anomalous FNMA low observation prevents asserting a clean independently verified rolling low. These are highly volatile OTC securities; volume on a favorable day does not establish that a large position can exit without market impact.

Fannie has 1,158,077,970 common shares outstanding at June30. Multiplying by US$2.34 gives approximately US$2.710 billion current common capitalization. That is not the fully diluted valuation of a recapitalized enterprise.

Treasury holds a warrant to acquire 79.9% of the common at a nominal exercise price. Ignoring all other issuance, current holders would retain approximately 20.1% after full exercise. Their US$2.710 billion market value therefore corresponds to approximately US$13.48 billion warrant-diluted common value, calculated. This does not include any new recapitalization shares, senior-preferred conversion, junior-preferred treatment or required fresh capital.

A simple earnings/price division is misleading. The company earns billions while the net-worth dividend directs value to Treasury. Treasury's US$117.1 billion senior preferred does not disappear as dividends are paid. Junior preferreds also rank ahead of common. Positive enterprise earnings do not imply a positive currently distributable common earnings stream.

A proper scenario model must specify policy/legal resolution, normalized earnings, required capital, recapitalization time, financing terms, senior and junior claims, and final share count. Only then can an ordinary equity multiple and discount rate be applied. No authenticated contemporaneous Ackman target or final capital plan is available at this cutoff.

The downside is not merely a lower P/E: wind-down, adverse policy, continued sweep or heavy dilution could leave common worth little even if mortgage finance remains profitable. The upside requires a favorable bridge from franchise value to this particular security, not just national need for the service.
docs.D05_political_and_market_worries.md:
Title: The administration and competing bills favor replacing the companies
Source: compiled from: https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2013/08/06/remarks-president-responsible-homeownership; https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/20130910_R43219_fbc0312cf2ec8be7526714c62ad2210d046573ec.html; https://www.politico.com/story/2013/07/fannie-freddie-mae-unite-ralph-nader-wall-street-093917
Date: 2013-09-10

The September10 Congressional Research Service report describes substantial housing-finance reform activity. The House PATH Act proposes winding down Fannie/Freddie and replacing their role with a utility that facilitates private securitization without a comparable government guarantee. The House Financial Services Committee ordered it reported July24.

The Senate Corker-Warner proposal also contemplates winding down the existing GSEs, but would replace them with a new federal mortgage-insurance structure. Private capital would absorb a meaningful first-loss layer before federal reinsurance responds. The proposals differ on government support while agreeing the current institutional arrangement should change.

President Obama's August6 Phoenix remarks support private capital at the center and winding down the existing enterprises. These are powerful counterweights to an investment case premised on simply restoring the old common-stock franchise unchanged.

Legislative proposals are not enacted law. Implementation would be complex because mortgage-market liquidity, the fixed-rate mortgage, affordable housing, taxpayer risk and financial stability all matter. A replacement system must attract capital and preserve functioning markets. Those obstacles may slow change but do not guarantee preservation of today's shareholders.

Politico's July10 report describes a coalition of hedge-fund investors and Ralph Nader seeking fair treatment for existing shareholders. This is evidence that the shareholder debate is active, not evidence that the coalition controls Congress or the administration.

The bull view is that profitable infrastructure would be expensive and risky to dismantle, and private capital may ultimately be needed in the existing organizations. The bear view is that policymakers can preserve the public function while changing the entities and allocating economics away from current common.

The Treasury warrant can create potential alignment with common appreciation, but Treasury also receives the senior dividend and can prioritize taxpayer recovery or policy. Its incentives are not identical to those of a minority holder who paid cash for common.

No scheduled vote, court date or administrative release guarantees resolution within a conventional activist holding period. The required patience may be long and politically driven. Common investors must separately price the chance, terms and timing of an outcome; “essential business” is not a sufficient catalyst.
docs.D06_contract_and_litigation.md:
Title: The net-worth dividend and contested shareholder remedies
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1026214/000119312512359938/d398152d8k.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/310522/000031052213000065/fanniemae201210k.htm; https://www.refinblog.com/fairholme-or-foul-investor-complaint-over-fannie-and-freddie-preferred/
Date: 2013-07-24

The August17 2012 third amendment changed the senior-preferred dividend mechanism. Beginning2013, the dividend generally equals net worth above the applicable capital reserve rather than the old fixed-rate amount. The capital reserve is US$3 billion in2013 and falls by US$600 million annually until zero in2018.

This removes the ability to retain ordinary positive earnings beyond the contractual reserve while the terms remain in force. It does not cancel the existing senior preferred. An investor cannot assume that cumulative dividends automatically repay the liquidation preference or terminate the agreement.

The amendment also accelerates reduction of retained investment portfolios toward US$250 billion by the end of2018. A valuation should distinguish the durable guarantee business from investment assets whose size policy requires to shrink.

Perry Capital and Fairholme initiated challenges in July2013. The publicly reported claims include statutory/administrative objections and constitutional takings arguments. A complaint is an allegation by a plaintiff, not a judicial finding that the sweep is illegal or that common shares must receive a particular recovery.

Cornell-affiliated law professor David Reiss's July24 commentary reviews Fairholme's complaint. It notes the argument that the amendment effectively created a new security after Treasury's purchase authority expired, but treats that as highly contested. He argues the government was already deeply involved through conservatorship, distinguishing the case from a straightforward seizure of an ordinary private company.

The commentary concludes shareholders face substantial legal difficulty even if their settled expectations were disrupted. This is an interpretation, not a forecast of a final judgment. Fairholme's preferred holdings also have different contractual priorities from common.

Legal routes can differ in plaintiffs, standing, governing law, remedies and timelines. Invalidating one action would not necessarily dictate immediate recapitalization, cash damages to all owners or release from conservatorship. A damages award, contract remedy and full common-equity restoration are distinct outcomes.

An investment model should not combine all favorable legal arguments as independent certainties or assume a near-term binary win. There may be years of litigation and appeals while profits continue flowing to Treasury. The key risk is inability to translate a plausible fairness argument into an enforceable, timely remedy benefiting the security actually purchased.
docs.D07_event_timeline.md:
Title: Improving earnings meet a hostile capital-allocation framework
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/310522/000031052213000138/a2013q2pressrelease.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1026214/000119312513323022/d554149dex991.htm; https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/20130910_R43219_fbc0312cf2ec8be7526714c62ad2210d046573ec.html; https://www.refinblog.com/fairholme-or-foul-investor-complaint-over-fannie-and-freddie-preferred/
Date: 2013-09-10

**September2008 — conservatorship.** FHFA assumes control and Treasury provides financial support through senior preferred agreements. The common remains outstanding but ordinary corporate governance and capital distributions are constrained.

**August17 2012 — third amendment.** Treasury/FHFA replace the fixed dividend with the net-worth-based mechanism effective2013. Capital buffers decline over time. Shareholders now face an explicit contractual barrier to retaining profits for ordinary recapitalization.

**April2013 — FY2012 report.** Fannie reports US$17.2 billion net income and expects continued profitability. The result confirms a substantial operating recovery but does not remove senior claims or the amended dividend.

**Q1 2013 results — deferred-tax recognition.** Fannie releases its valuation allowance, producing an approximately US$50.6 billion income-tax benefit. This explains why headline profits greatly exceed a normal recurring earnings run rate.

**June/July — legislative proposals.** Corker-Warner and the PATH Act outline different replacement systems. They create genuine wind-down risk without establishing an enacted final settlement.

**July — shareholder lawsuits.** Perry and Fairholme challenge the amended arrangement through different legal theories. Their actions demonstrate available arguments, not a favorable ruling.

**August6 — presidential housing remarks.** The administration supports winding down the existing enterprises and putting private capital at the center of a reformed mortgage system.

**August7–8 — Q2 results.** Freddie reports US$5.0 billion net income; Fannie reports US$10.1 billion. Both forecast large September Treasury dividends and retain unchanged senior-preferred balances.

**September10 — CRS comparison.** The report clarifies the key differences between House and Senate proposals and the substantial common objective of replacing the current arrangement.

By October31, the core tension remains unresolved: profitable national franchises coexist with highly constrained common claims. The next quarterly results are not yet public. No final court outcome, amended sweep, capital-retention permission, relisting timetable or completed release is an available fact.

A prospective shareholder can monitor profits, credit, legal proceedings and policy proposals. These are observable milestones but not a date-certain control catalyst. The event sequence supports a contingent-value analysis rather than treating the position like a normal operating turnaround.
docs.D08_pershing_square_context.md:
Title: Capital capacity and competing legal/activist exposures
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1336528/000117266113001220/0001172661-13-001220.txt; https://www.reuters.com/article/world/ackman-s-pershing-square-cuts-herbalife-stock-short-position-idUSBRE9911AZ/; https://archive.nytimes.com/dealbook.nytimes.com/2013/10/03/ackman-modifies-bet-against-herbalife/
Date: 2013-10-03

Reuters's October3 report describes Pershing Square as managing approximately US$11 billion. That is a contemporary approximate manager figure, not an exact October31 fund NAV or cash balance.

The latest 13F is the June30 report filed August14. It shows US$10.951937 billion table value, but US$1.924750 billion relates to P&G calls reported using underlying-share value, not cash premium or NAV exposure. The table must not be used as a direct fully invested portfolio or liquidity reconciliation.

| Aggregated position | June table value, US$m |
|---|---:|
| Canadian Pacific common | 2,932.527 |
| General Growth common | 1,346.970 |
| Beam common | 1,313.859 |
| Air Products common | 924.464 |
| Burger King common | 748.640 |
| P&G common | 688.301 |
| JCP common | 667.414 |
| Howard Hughes common | 399.939 |
| Matson common | 5.073 |
| P&G calls, underlying-share value | 1,924.750 |

Sole/shared rows are aggregated once. These are stale June marks, not current weights. JCP has since been exited publicly; the June line should not be treated as remaining exposure in October. GGP and Howard Hughes demonstrate real-estate and restructuring experience, while Canadian Pacific and Air Products represent corporate operating/change opportunities.

The October3 reporting says more than40% of the Herbalife stock short was reduced/replaced in part with derivatives, reflecting position-management risk after adverse price moves. Ackman maintains his thesis; Herbalife disputes it. This consumes attention and introduces a different regulatory/legal exposure from mortgage finance.

A new policy-dependent common investment would therefore sit alongside concentrated public positions and an ongoing public short campaign. Capital may be available, but the latest filing does not reveal unrestricted cash or exposure to correlated legal disappointments.

No authenticated public Ackman statement endorsing Fannie/Freddie common is available in this pre-disclosure snapshot. A model should form its own view from the business and security waterfall rather than infer conviction from a subsequent campaign. The possible engagement tools are public advocacy and legal/policy work, not ordinary board-control activism.

drivers.driver: Essential guarantee infrastructure and the prepayable30-year fixed mortgage cannot readily be replaced.
drivers.quote: there is no credible alternative to replace them

drivers.driver: Challenge the sweep and restore a route from enterprise profits to shareholder value; this is Ackman's position, not a final legal holding.
drivers.quote: We view this net worth sweep as an unlawful taking of shareholders’ private property

drivers.driver: Recapitalize and eventually release the enterprises; Treasury warrant ownership could align taxpayer upside with common.
drivers.source: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2025/01/16112701/Fannie-Mae-Freddie-Mac-01-16-2025-Presentation.pdf (2025-01-16 later detailed thesis, not an entry-date model)

drivers.driver: Large potential valuation gap conditional on capital structure and policy; later2014 US$23–47 scenarios must not be imported as2013 prices or realized returns.

answer_key.pack_quality_notes: Eight docs, latest publishedQ2 only. Strong sweep/warrant distinction, contemporaneous contrary policy and legal opinion, two-enterprise operating comparison. Annual net revenue/CFO/capital details and clean rolling low remain explicit gaps. No futureQ3 tax event, lawsuits outcome, Ackman targets or trade disclosure in docs.

valuation.entry_multiple: N/A - P/E not meaningful due to net-worth sweep [D02, D04]
valuation.eps_path: Profitability has returned with six consecutive profitable quarters [D03], though EPS is currently fully diverted by the net-worth sweep [D01, D06].
valuation.downside_case: Total loss of capital if the GSEs are liquidated and common equity is extinguished [D04, D05].

drivers.driver: The underlying business is an essential and dominant piece of the US housing infrastructure, currently demonstrating a return to consistent profitability [D01, D03].
The market incorrectly views the government's conservatorship and net-worth sweep as a permanent, terminal impairment of value, failing to price the option value of shareholder rights [D01, D05].
Active shareholder litigation and potential legislative shifts provide a pathway to challenge government overreach and restore access to the firm's earnings power [D06, D07].
The current equity valuation is highly asymmetric, offering significant upside relative to the downside of a total loss should legal or political resolution prove favorable [D05, D06].

kill_criteria: Legislative passage of a GSE wind-down bill that explicitly prioritizes Treasury interests and wipes out common shareholders [D05].
Judicial ruling in Fairholme or Perry Capital litigation that upholds the government's authority to conduct the net-worth sweep indefinitely [D06].
FHFA or Treasury takes specific steps to execute a plan that definitively precludes any path for common shareholder participation in future recapitalization [D02, D05].
final.what_would_change_our_mind: A definitive judicial or legislative ruling that confirms the government's permanent, unchecked right to extract all economic value from the entity for the Treasury, rendering common equity essentially worthless.
final.memo:
Fannie Mae is a dominant, essential pillar of the American housing market, providing the scale and infrastructure necessary for liquid mortgage issuance [D01]. Despite the current government-mandated conservatorship, the company has proven its fundamental vitality by generating six consecutive quarters of profitability [D03]. This is a business that, absent regulatory distortion, would be a core, high-quality, free-cash-flow-generative financial institution [D01, D03].

Today, the market has mispriced this asset as having zero value, operating under the assumption that the government’s current trajectory will inevitably lead to a total wipeout of common equity [D01, D05]. We believe the market is wrong to ignore the significant legal and political tension currently building, which provides a meaningful, if binary, opportunity for the restoration of shareholder rights [D05, D06].

While traditional valuation metrics like P/E are not currently meaningful due to the net-worth sweep, we evaluate this as a high-alpha, asymmetric option on the normalization of the GSEs [D02, D04]. The potential for a favorable legal resolution in pending litigation or a change in legislative stance represents a catalyst that could unlock substantial value from current distressed levels [D06, D07].

Our role is to support the ongoing legal challenges and engage with stakeholders to ensure that any reform preserves the rights of common shareholders rather than prioritizing a total wind-down [D05, D06]. We are prepared to use the tools of activism to defend the intrinsic value of this irreplaceable business [D06, D07].

We recognize the risks: the primary threat is a government-led liquidation that leaves nothing for common shareholders [D04, D05]. However, the current valuation reflects a complete disregard for the probability of a more equitable resolution [D04].

We are initiating a 5% position in the common equity [D05]. This is an asymmetric bet on the integrity of the law and the future of the American housing finance system, which we view as one of the most compelling risk-reward setups in our current universe [D06, D07].

valuation.entry_multiple: N/A (distressed asset pricing based on litigation/political optionality rather than P/E multiple [D04, D06])
valuation.eps_path: Not applicable (earnings are currently swept to Treasury [D06, D07])
valuation.downside_case: The investment loses 100% of its value if the courts uphold the Net Worth Sweep and the government proceeds with the liquidation of the enterprise [D04, D06].

drivers.driver: Fannie Mae is a critical financial utility that remains the essential backbone of the U.S. housing market [D01].
The market incorrectly views the common equity as having zero value, ignoring the substantial intrinsic value of the guarantee franchise [D03, D06].
Pending litigation provides a clear legal path to challenge the Net Worth Sweep and restore shareholder rights to retained earnings [D06].
The company remains highly profitable, demonstrating that the underlying business is economically viable once capital constraints are normalized [D03].

kill_criteria: Courts definitively rule that the Net Worth Sweep is legal and the FHFA has absolute authority over equity [D06].
Legislative action formally liquidates the enterprise without shareholder compensation [D05].
The core guarantee franchise ceases to be profitable [D03].
final.what_would_change_our_mind: A definitive judicial or legislative determination that confirms the permanent expropriation of shareholder equity and the exclusion of private capital from the GSEs.
final.memo:
Fannie Mae represents an essential component of the American housing finance system, providing vital liquidity by guaranteeing residential mortgages [D01]. While the company is currently under conservatorship, it maintains a dominant competitive position backed by insurmountable barriers to entry, including deep lender relationships and proprietary data infrastructure [D01]. Despite the constraints of the conservatorship, the core guarantee business continues to generate significant profits [D03].

We believe the current market valuation drastically misprices the equity by assuming a perpetual state of liquidation and total seizure of shareholder value under the Net Worth Sweep [D06]. The market has incorrectly concluded that the government’s present control equates to a permanent termination of private rights [D06]. In reality, the legal standing of shareholders remains a critical issue currently being addressed in the courts [D06].

Our assessment is based on the potential for successful litigation to overturn the Net Worth Sweep and allow for the rebuilding of capital [D06]. Assuming a successful resolution, we believe a re-privatized entity could command a normalized earnings multiple of approximately 8x, suggesting substantial upside from current distressed trading levels [D03, D06]. While the bear case involves a total loss of capital, the asymmetric risk-reward profile is compelling [D04, D06].

Our role is to advocate for a policy shift that moves the enterprises away from a liquidation trajectory toward a viable, re-privatized capital structure [D05, D06]. We will actively support legal efforts to protect shareholder rights and clarify the limits of the FHFA’s conservatorship authority [D06]. By demonstrating the essential utility value of the franchise, we aim to build a consensus for reform [D03, D05].

Risks remain high, particularly regarding political volatility and the potential for the PATH Act or similar legislation to finalize a liquidation [D05, D06]. We are prepared to exit the position if the courts definitively validate the Net Worth Sweep or if the core franchise loses its fundamental profitability [D03, D06].

We are initiating a 2% position, with a target size of 5% of NAV, reflecting the speculative, event-driven nature of this investment [D04, D06].
uncited_claims: We believe a re-privatized entity could command a normalized earnings multiple of approximately 8x.
